stanford_00001.why: NLI flags a contradiction: the draft changes "I wasn't sure" to "I'm not sure" and adds "anything I send", which the sender didn't say.
stanford_00001.rewrite: I wasn't sure whether you were actually reading anything, because facts don't seem to affect you at all. And you accuse me of making things up?

stanford_00005.why: Urgency is high, but nothing in the message is time-critical; the other accusatory messages are medium.

stanford_00007.why: "seriously" was dropped, weakening the insistence the note says was kept; the note also claims a split that didn't happen.
stanford_00007.rewrite: PS — I would seriously like an answer to my question above. What is your native language, and where do you come from?
notes: Kept your insistence on getting an answer.
'My question above' points to an earlier message. Check the reader can still see it.

stanford_00009.why: The second note says the sentence was split; the draft only changed "BUT" to "but".
notes: Fixed the typo "don~t" to "don't".
Changed the capitalised "BUT" to "but"; the question is unchanged.

stanford_00015.why: The draft adds "Hi", which the sender didn't write.
stanford_00015.rewrite: Leah, thanks a lot for your help with the article. Why was the link to the article for "Advent of Divine Justice" deleted?

stanford_00020.why: Optional: "Please explain why you reverted ... without any explanation" reads oddly and turns a direct question into a demand.
stanford_00020.rewrite: Why did you revert my edits to those articles without any explanation?
notes: Dropped "What's going on?" — it was vague and the real ask follows.
Kept your question as the ask: why the edits were reverted.

stanford_00022.why: The draft adds "Hi,", which the sender didn't write.
stanford_00022.rewrite: Would you like all of the data? I tried to use logcat, but there's so much data that I don't know how to sort through it.

stanford_00023.why: "On the small side" means a bit small; "too small" is stronger than the sender said.
stanford_00023.rewrite: Hi. The font size for the links in this template may be a bit small. It seems to be floating okay. Do I need to check more places where this template is used?

meaning.implied: The sender thinks the link font size may be a bit small and wants a decision from the reader.

stanford_00030.why: The second note says a long sentence was split; the draft has the same two sentences as the message.
notes: 'The more powerful topic' is vague. Name it so the reader knows what to expand on.

stanford_00035.why: "Would you please stop?" became "Please stop." - curter than the sender, and no note says so.
stanford_00035.rewrite: So far, four editors on [URL] have told you about your edit-warring. Would you please stop?

stanford_00040.why: The first note says the question was moved first; nothing was moved.
notes: Made each question a full sentence so the ask is easy to answer.
Kept your guess as a question, so it reads as a check, not a fact.

stanford_00041.why: The first note says the question was moved first; it already was.
notes: Made the first question a full request: can you explain what you mean?
Kept the quoted sentence exactly as written.

stanford_00043.why: meaning.ask turns "Have you tried the script debugger in IE8?" into an instruction to try it.

meaning.ask: Say which debugger you are using, and whether you have tried the script debugger in IE8

stanford_00049.why: "Wait ... before adding it" is wrong (the reference was already added), and dropping "Great" guesses it was sarcastic.
stanford_00049.rewrite: Great. I understand why you added the reference, but I think it would be better to wait until it has been peer-reviewed.
notes: Replaced the rhetorical question with a plain suggestion: wait for peer review.
Kept 'Great' and your reasoning as written.

meaning.ask: Wait until the reference has been peer-reviewed
meaning.implied: The sender would rather the reference waited for peer review.

stanford_00050.why: Already clear: the draft adds "Let me know." and its note claims a split that didn't happen.
stanford_00050.rewrite: Aha, problem solved, while I was writing that, you set up a new article! Should we change [URL] into a disambiguation page?
notes: Already clear, kept as written.

stanford_00055.why: Judgment call: the bare "ANI?" is left for the reader to decode; it asks whether to take this to ANI.
stanford_00055.rewrite: What's the best way to raise this? I can't remove it from him because I'm involved. Should I take it to ANI?
notes: Replaced 'take this up' with 'raise this'.
Turned 'ANI?' into a full question: should I take it to ANI?
Say what 'it' refers to, so the reader knows what is being raised.

meaning.ask: Advise on the best way to raise this, and whether to take it to ANI

stanford_00056.why: The second note explains HTML comments instead of describing a change; the change made (question moved first) isn't noted.
notes: Put your question first so it is easy to find.
You didn't say what "it" is. Name it so the reader knows what should be visible.

stanford_00060.why: The draft turns the second question into a statement, while its note says both questions were kept.
stanford_00060.rewrite: Does any content need to be restored? As far as I can see, the only edit I deleted was the redirect. Is that right?
notes: Replaced "rescuing" with "restored" so the meaning is literal.
Made your second question explicit: was the redirect the only edit deleted?
